title: Unify async runtime: standardize retry/failure semantics across Redis Streams and Kafka adapters
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Summary:
We have divergent retry, failure and visibility semantics between the Redis-backed list workers (legacy) and the newer Kafka consumer adapters. This causes unpredictable duplicate work, inconsistent dead-letter handling, and makes rollouts fragile when we route work across adapters. The goal of this ticket is to create a single, well-documented failure model and implement it in both adapters: Redis (migrating list consumers where needed to Redis Streams/consumer groups) and Kafka.

Motivation / Why now:
- Multiple incidents in the last quarter where in-flight retries caused token-cost spikes and duplicate downstream side effects.
- Ops complexity when debugging: different tools, different dashboards, inconsistent metrics and DLQ signals.
- Upcoming Dedicated customer committed to predictable at-least-once semantics across private deployments.

Non-goals:
- Full rework of application-level idempotency (that is owned by product teams). We will provide helpers and conventions but not enforce idempotency across all handlers.

Scope:
- Define canonical retry/failure lifecycle (visibility lease, retry count and backoff, DLQ semantics, tombstone/poison handling).
- Implement a small compatibility shim so existing Redis list workers keep running during migration (graceful draining).
- Add Redis Streams consumer-group implementation for high-throughput paths and wire up the shared retry metadata envelope.
- Harmonize metrics and tracing tags so Console can show unified per-route retry/success/failure rates.
technical_approach: Design a canonical message envelope: metadata fields (attempt, first_seen_ts, idempotency_key, original_queue, handler_version). Store as JSON in payload wrapper.

Introduce a visibility-lease concept for Redis lists: implement a lightweight lease manager with a short-lived lease token to mimic consumer commit semantics. This will be a compatibility layer until Streams are fully adopted.
Implement Redis Streams consumer-group as the default for new high-throughput queues. Use XGROUP/XREADGROUP semantics to support explicit ACKs and pending entries list (PEL) for retries.

Standardize retry strategy: configurable per-queue policy (max_attempts, backoff_strategy: linear|exp|jitter, retry_window_ms). Default: max_attempts=5, backoff=exponential with full jitter starting at 500ms.

Dead-letter queue policy: messages past max_attempts are written to a DLQ topic/stream with original envelope and failure metadata. DLQ consumers will be a separate workflow with stricter access controls.
Introduce a per-queue circuit-breaker and soft-queue-shed flag in the queue config to prevent cascading downstream failures. Circuit state surfaced to Console and to the routing logic.
Add instrumentation: retry_count histogram, attempts_per_message, time_to_deadletter, pending_entries_size. Create Grafana/Console dashboards and tracing spans for attempt start/end/ack/fail.
Provide lightweight client libraries (Go/Node) for creating the canonical envelope and helper functions to ACK/RETRY/DLQ messages to reduce app-level boilerplate.

Migration plan: start with non-customer-facing low-volume queues, iterate, then migrate high-throughput workers by switching the adapter and enabling Streams on a per-queue basis. Provide toggle for rollout and automatic fallback to legacy list shim.
Add unit & integration tests simulating rebalances, crashes, message duplication, and network partitions. Add chaos tests that kill worker processes while messages are in-flight.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical message envelope is defined and published in the infra-queues spec doc (link in docs_and_links).
Redis Streams adapter implements ACK, REJECT (with DLQ write), and requeue-with-backoff behavior aligned with the canonical spec.
Legacy Redis-list shim exists and can be enabled per-queue; no production route is disabled without a rolling migration plan.
Console shows unified retry/success/failure metrics for at least three migrated queues and dashboard panels for retry latency and DLQ rates.
Automated tests cover visibility lease expiry, worker crash + pending-entry reclamation, and DLQ write verification.
Documentation and client helper libraries are published in the repo and linked from the infra-queues README.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): implement spec and Streams adapter. Run against 2 low-risk internal queues for 1 week with enhanced monitoring.
Phase 2 (Expand): migrate 6 medium-volume queues. Enable circuit-breaker defaults and DLQ retention policies. Run 2-week validation window.
Phase 3 (High-volume): migrate top 3 throughput queues during low-traffic windows with blue/green worker rollouts and the list-shim fallback enabled.
Rollback: toggle queue back to legacy list-shim adapter and flush temporary leases. Notify on-call and open a rollback incident runbook entry.
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope serialization/deserialization and header-preservation across adapters.
Integration test that simulates worker crash: produce 100 messages, crash consumer mid-processing, ensure pending entries are reclaimed and processed once more without loss of metadata.
Chaos test that kills network to Redis/Kafka for short windows and validates backoff + circuit-breaker behavior.
Load test on Streams adapter to verify throughput parity with existing list-based workers and measure latency regression (target <10% regression).
notes: We intentionally keep application idempotency as a responsibility of product teams. The infra work adds clear tooling and examples to make it straightforward for handler authors.
